chunks: It is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, Abū al-ʿAbbās, and ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man comes to own his parents, or his sister, or his paternal aunt, or his maternal aunt, or his brother’s daughter, or his sister’s daughter—and he mentioned the women of this verse—then they all become free. A man may own his paternal uncle, his brother’s son, his sister’s son, and his maternal uncle; but he may not own his mother through nursing, nor his sister, nor his paternal aunt, nor his maternal aunt. If he comes to own them, they are emancipated.
He عليه السلام said: Whatever is prohibited among women by lineage is likewise prohibited by nursing.
And he عليه السلام said: He may own males except the father and the son, and he may not own any woman who is a mahram.
I said: And does the same apply in nursing? He عليه السلام said: Yes, the like of that applies in nursing.

key_terms.الرَّضَاعَةِ: nursing relationship that establishes legal kinship
key_terms.ذَاتَ مَحْرَمٍ: a woman within the permanently unmarriageable kin category
key_terms.عَتَقُوا: they became free or were emancipated
key_terms.مَلَكَ: to come into legal ownership or possession

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on owning close relatives or milk-relatives in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings on ownership and emancipation involving close blood and milk relatives. It establishes that certain mahram women, as well as parents and children, cannot remain in ownership and are freed upon acquisition, and that the prohibitions of lineage extend likewise to nursing relationships.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3435 - It is narrated from Abu Basir, Abu al-Abbas, and Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"If a man owns his parents, or his sister, or his paternal aunt, or his maternal aunt, or his brother's daughter, or his sister's daughter"-and he mentioned the women listed in this verse-"then they all become free.
However, a man may own his paternal uncle, or his brother's son, or his sister's son, or his maternal uncle, but he may not own his mother through nursing, nor his sister, nor his paternal aunt, nor his maternal aunt. If he comes to own them, they are freed."
Imam (as) also said: "What is prohibited due to lineage among women is also prohibited through nursing."
And Imam (as) said: "A man may own males except his father and his son, and he may not own any woman who is a mahram."

I said: "Does the same ruling apply in the case of nursing?"
Imam (as) said: "Yes, the same rulingapplies in the case of nursing."
